description: Heritage `value of … for key` on a LIST container raises the byte-identical Core `ol-type` the dotted `:scores.tom` selector raises — `expected: "dict"`, `operation: "field"`, message "field needs a dict, but got a list." — and NOT the `[key]` selector's `expected: "list or dict"`. This fixture is issue #784's regression: with the `[key]` expectation the reader told a learner "index needs a list or dict, but got a list", naming as required a type the offending value already had. The list container is the one type that exposes it — `number`, `word`, and `boolean` sit outside `"list or dict"`, so the WRONG params still read sensibly for them, which is why the previous corpus never caught it: every fixture that EXECUTED the reader used a dict container, except the single one that used a number. The reader is dict-only (`spec/data-structures.md:268` types its operand `dictExpr`), so `:scores.tom` — not `:scores["tom"]`, which indexes lists and would reject the KEY instead — is its Core twin; `spec/conformance.md:146` requires that twin's params exactly, since Heritage is alternate spellings only, no new semantics. NO Heritage spelling appears in any payload (`operation` is the Core `"field"`, never `"value of"` — issue #670). The span points at the reader's `:scores` operand, the analog of the selector's own span (localization-only difference — `spec/localization.md`). Heritage depends on Data (`spec/conformance.md:301`), so both `data` and `heritage` are active.
